page: Microsoft Azure D4ps_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine built on the arm64 architecture and managed via the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance features 4 physical cores and 4 vCPUs with a 1:1 thread-to-core mapping, driven by dedicated ARM Neoverse-N2 silicon clocked at 3.4 GHz. Cache sizing comprises 64 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 128 MB L3 cache pool. System memory totals 16.0 GB, maintaining a balanced 4.0 GB per vCPU allocation ratio. No local disk storage or dedicated GPUs are bundled with this instance type, requiring external remote block storage for persistent data requirements.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent mid-tier execution across typical compute and system operations. Single-threaded gzip compression performs in the top quartile at 32.94 GB/sec, and the PassMark memory evaluation shows solid memory subsystem throughput with a score of 2757.46. Large-block memory bandwidth measures 88.86 GB/sec for reads and 38.79 GB/sec for writes. Conversely, vector-heavy and specialized tasks exhibit clear performance limits: Geekbench ray tracing and image processing register in the bottom quartile, and the PassMark encryption benchmark drops to the bottom 10% with a score of 750.06.

Given its ARM-based architecture and absence of attached local NVMe storage, the D4ps_v6 provides an efficient compute profile for non-vectorized enterprise workloads. Core throughput is well matched to standard application hosting, static web serving (measured at 8.27 GB/sec), Clang software compilation, and in-memory caches like Redis, which reached 8.36 million set operations per second.
description: Microsoft Azure D4ps_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by 4 dedicated ARM Neoverse-N2 cores running at 3.4 GHz on the arm64 architecture. Configured with a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio, it includes 16.0 GB of RAM alongside 128 MB of L3 cache, with no integrated local storage or GPU hardware. In benchmark tests, the instance shows strong results in memory throughput and single-threaded gzip compression, alongside average performance in compilation, static web serving, and Redis operations. However, performance trails in cryptographic routines, ray tracing, and image processing tasks that demand dedicated vector or matrix extensions. Operating without local disks, the D4ps_v6 is structured for general enterprise utility, containerized backends, software builds, and standard web serving environments relying on networked storage.
